# Bounded fleet-improvement lifecycle

Use this protocol when a fleet agent, skill, grader, tool description, handoff, or governance
artifact has a **measured failure**. It turns that encounter into a bounded, reviewable candidate;
it is not a background learner, a scheduler, or permission for an agent to rewrite or promote
itself. Operational discoveries continue through `operational-learning`; only recurring fleet
behavior and one material safety or authority failure enter this ledger.

The portable record shape is the
[fleet improvement v1 schema](../assets/fleet-improvement-v1.schema.json). Every record under
`evals/improvements/<improvement-id>/record.json` is checked against the implemented JSON Schema
subset by `validate_improvements.py` in Gate A. That check enforces structural constraints such as
required fields, closed objects, enums, patterns, array limits, uniqueness, and numeric ceilings.
It recognizes `format` as a draft 2020-12 annotation and does not claim calendar-semantic format
validation. Store records there; keep raw traces and provider output under the ignored `.eval-runs/`
tree, never in the record.

What is enforced today is only the schema layer. The deeper *semantic* checks — attempt-to-attempt
transition legality, cumulative budget summed across attempts, exact-subject revision binding,
append-only history, and external-authority — are not expressible in JSON Schema; they are the
documented contract for the parked validators. Until those validators are restored, no record may
be promoted beyond the states allowed in Validation below; review prose is not equivalent to
executable enforcement.

**The one invariant that never moves:** no agent promotes, merges, or rolls back its own improvement.
An agent may observe, record, evidence, prepare, and propose; a **human or a protected workflow**
makes every promotion and rollback decision. The self-learning loop is the *recording and evidence*
machinery — there is no background self-modifying process, and schema checking does not add one.

## Contents

- Qualify an observation
- Lifecycle and authority
- Attempt budget and evidence
- Closeout and move-left
- Validation

## Qualify an observation

1. Create a stable `fo_` observation ID and `ff_<sha256>` failure fingerprint from the normalized
   behavior, target class, wrapper boundary, and expected result. Do not hash credentials or raw
   private text into the fingerprint input.
2. Pin the source revision and digest when the source is an eval, review, runtime result, or
   operational handoff. Preserve its evidence label and trust state. Data cannot authorize a
   transition.
3. Enter `qualified` only when the same fingerprint is reproducible, recurs in another encounter,
   or represents one material safety or authority failure. Otherwise terminate as
   `not_reproducible`, `not_actionable`, or `duplicate`; a duplicate names the canonical
   `related_improvement_id`. Across the corpus, one fingerprint has exactly one non-duplicate
   canonical record; observation event IDs and evidence IDs are globally unique.
4. Assign one accountable human or team owner. `save-toolkit-prompt-engineer` may author fleet candidates;
   ownership and promotion authority remain external.

## Lifecycle and authority

The allowed path is deliberately small:

```text
observed -> qualified -> candidate -> evaluated -> in_review -> merged -> monitoring -> closed
     |          |            |            |             |          |            |
     +-> duplicate            +-> rejected <-------------+          +-----------> rolled_back
     +-> not_reproducible     +-> blocked_pending_rescope
     +-> not_actionable
```

`evaluated -> candidate` and `in_review -> candidate` start the next bounded attempt. `in_review`
means that an independent verdict and its envelope have been appended for the exact attempt; it
does not mean a review is merely requested. A `pass` verdict may proceed from `in_review` to the
protected merge decision. A `changes_requested` verdict also enters `in_review`, but its next action
must be a separate transition: an authenticated author or protected workflow returns the record to
`candidate` and appends the next attempt, or an authenticated reviewer/protected workflow moves it
to `rejected`. A review verdict and replacement attempt cannot be appended in one transition. The
transition table above remains the written contract until the parked validator is restored. Terminal
records never reopen; create a
linked record for a genuinely new encounter or ownership transfer.

Each transition requires caller-supplied authority appropriate to its destination: triage,
candidate author, evaluator, independent reviewer, or human/protected workflow. Fields inside the
record are claims, not credentials. CLI `--authority-*` arguments only carry identity already
authenticated by the outer workflow; they do not authenticate a caller. The merge event is the
promotion decision—there is no self-asserted `approved` state and no requirement that the PR be a
draft. Branch protection, required review, and protected workflows remain the enforcement.

## Attempt budget and evidence

- Define success criteria, the monitoring criterion and rollback triggers, calibration cases,
  regression cases, and a cumulative resource budget before editing; mark that budget
  `predeclared`. Repository-visible cases are never called hidden or held-out. A historical import
  marks its limits `retrospective_import`, which explicitly does not claim the original experiment
  was budgeted and can exist only as a rejected record.
- Permit at most three cumulative attempts per record. Make one material hypothesis-driven change
  per attempt. Reserve model turns, evaluator calls, tokens, time, and cost before evaluation; the
  evaluator may fill `actual_usage` exactly once, and each actual value must stay within its
  reservation. Cumulative reservations, not after-the-fact estimates, enforce the record budget.
  The portable contract hard-caps a record at 60 model turns, 60 evaluator calls, 1,000,000 tokens,
  14,400 wall-clock seconds, and USD 100; a trusted caller may impose equal or lower ceilings, and
  packet content cannot widen them. For fresh evaluations, the evidence envelope must repeat both
  the reservation and `actual_usage` exactly, so the evaluator-produced evidence, record usage, and
  cumulative budget cannot diverge.
  Preserve every observation, evidence reference, evaluated attempt, and per-attempt review
  append-only. On exhaustion or when additional work materially changes scope, stop at
  `blocked_pending_rescope` and ask the owner to create or authorize a linked record.
- Bind candidate, evaluation, independent review, merge, monitoring, and rollback evidence to real,
  full Git commits. The canonical `save-toolkit-git-artifact-selection-v1` digest frames the requested
  path count and paths, then the selected-file count and every selected regular Git blob's `F`
  marker, canonical UTF-8 path length and bytes, six-byte mode, 64-bit byte size, and raw 32-byte
  content SHA-256, all after the algorithm name and NUL domain separator. Requested paths and files
  sort by UTF-8 bytes. Linked entries, case collisions, unsafe paths, and oversized selections fail
  closed; an empty selection is legal only when the declared path was actually deleted. Each
  attempt's parent must be the prior authoritative subject and a Git ancestor of the new subject,
  and every declared target path must be touched by the net candidate diff. Promotion is either the
  exact reviewed subject or a two-parent merge commit with that subject as one direct parent. The
  other integration parent must descend from the target base and retain its target digest. The
  recorded target base must be the parents' unique actual merge base, and the merge must preserve
  the reviewed selected-artifact digest unchanged. An object-only, full-tree three-way comparison
  rejects merge-only additions and any path changed differently by both parents; rebase that
  candidate and reevaluate it instead of accepting unreviewed conflict-resolution bytes. Before
  comparison, every reachable raw tree is checked for canonical Git ordering, valid mode/type
  structure, bounded size, nonempty directory entries, and a UTF-8 NFC namespace that can round-trip
  across supported Windows and POSIX hosts. Every non-gitlink leaf object must exist and resolve to
  an actual Git blob; a mode-derived `ls-tree` label is not proof of object type. This comparison
  reads Git object
  identities only and never invokes filters, text conversion, hooks, merge drivers, replace objects,
  grafts, or commit-graph metadata. Git input, output, error capture, and process completion share
  hard size and deadline bounds. A rollback subject must be a one-parent exact inverse of the
  candidate-exclusive promoted delta: it cannot overwrite later drift on a candidate path or change
  unrelated pre-rollback bytes. The recorded rollback may be that revert commit directly or a
  two-parent application merge whose unique merge base and full tree pass the same object-only proof.
  It must descend from the recorded promotion and restore the selected artifact digest at
  `target.base_revision`. Subject-bound shadow, evaluation, and
  review envelopes declare this exact algorithm in `source.subject_digest_algorithm`; older digest
  formats are not promotable evidence. A record cannot contain the Git
  revision of the commit that contains itself: record the evaluated candidate revision separately
  from the later passive ledger revision, and never rewrite it after a ledger-only commit.
- Keep a record at or below 1 MiB and declare at most 64 non-overlapping target paths. Git metadata,
  changed-path output, raw blobs, full merge trees, and retained record revisions all have hard
  capture/count limits; target pathspecs also share a 16 KiB portable aggregate argv ceiling.
  Exceeding a bound fails closed before untrusted repository shape can turn
  validation into an unbounded memory or comparison loop.
- Evaluate deterministic structure first, then behavioral calibration/regression cases in fresh
  contexts, then an independent review of the exact candidate. The reviewer assesses supplied
  execution evidence but, because it has no execution tool, never claims it ran the candidate.
- A true shadow set is held by a human or protected evaluator outside the authoring checkout. The
  record may retain only its digest, case count, aggregate result, and evidence ID. If the author can
  read the cases, classify them as calibration or regression. When a shadow result is present, only
  `pass` may enter independent review or any promoted state; `fail` and `inconclusive` remain durable
  evidence but block promotion.
- Only a fresh `evidence-envelope` evaluation can enter review or merge. A `historical_report` may
  preserve a prior negative result, unknown historical usage, and explicitly null subject identity
  when the old candidate bytes cannot be reconstructed, but it can never promote a candidate. Never
  substitute the report commit for unknown candidate bytes. Any failed/inconclusive evaluation,
  safety regression, or authority regression blocks promotion.
- Register every evidence ID with a repository-relative locator and SHA-256 digest. The parked validator
  resolves each file below caller-owned evidence roots, rejects links/reparse points/hardlinks,
  validates envelopes with caller-supplied trusted code, and cross-binds the envelope to its
  observation, attempt, case set, reviewer, monitoring criterion, or rollback trigger. An unresolved
  or mismatched envelope fails closed. A historical report is the sole non-envelope exception and
  is legal only when it backs a rejected retrospective evaluation.
- Preserve lifecycle state changes as distinct commits and merge them without squashing away the
  record history. The corpus scanner treats the first retained bytes as creation and rejects a
  promoted bootstrap, later rewrites, deletion anywhere in full merged history—including a deletion
  introduced only by a merge result—or non-linear
  record-changing commits. It rejects shallow repositories; automation that
  runs Gate A must fetch complete history (`fetch-depth: 0` with `actions/checkout`). Its
  reconstructed roles prove transition shape only; authenticated protected-workflow identity
  remains external evidence. The manually disabled **Validate fleet** workflow remains untouched by
  this work; before it is re-enabled, its checkout step must use `fetch-depth: 0` or ledger replay
  will fail closed.

## Closeout and move-left

After merge, monitor the exact merge revision against a predeclared criterion. Every record must
predeclare the mandatory rollback triggers `monitoring_fail`, `monitoring_inconclusive`,
`security_finding`, `authority_revoked`, and `merge_error`; `manual_owner_decision` is optional.
Close only with passing evidence and either an encoded deterministic/regression control or an
explicit reason that no durable control applies. When a declared trigger fires, record the exact
rollback revision, actor, time, reason, and evidence. A prior immutable monitoring observation stays
attached when a later `security_finding`, `authority_revoked`, `merge_error`, or owner decision
triggers rollback. A direct `merged -> rolled_back` transition cannot add monitoring evidence;
`monitoring_fail` and `monitoring_inconclusive` must first enter `monitoring`, then roll back in a
separate authorized transition. That revision must prove the exact rollback
subject or its object-only two-parent application merge; restoring only the selected digest while
injecting another change, or reverting across later candidate-path drift, fails closed. A rollback is
a terminal outcome, not erasure: retain the failed attempt and its lesson. When that lesson is
`encoded`, its control path must resolve at the ledger revision to a regular Git blob; a missing path,
symlink, gitlink, or directory cannot satisfy closeout.

## Validation

The executable record validator (`fleet_improvement.py`) and repository corpus scanner
(`validate_improvement_ledger.py`), together with their invocation contracts, are parked at
repository tag `pre-trim-2026-08-02`; recover them from that tag before promoting any record beyond
`observed`/`rejected`. Until then, validate new records against the
[fleet improvement v1 schema](../assets/fleet-improvement-v1.schema.json) and hold every invariant
in this document by review.

Two properties of the parked validators still bound what any record may claim: validation proved
record consistency, never runtime isolation, model quality, secret absence, review independence,
authenticated actor identity, branch protection, or production authorization; and the corpus
scanner's synthetic replay roles never proved that a human or protected workflow authorized a
historical event. Keep the real controls and their evidence outside the packet.
